executiveSummaryMd: The exercise tested the airport's response to a cyber incident that compromised the Flight Information Display System (FIDS), Baggage Handling System (BHS), and Public Address (PA) system, leading to misinformation, passenger confusion, and safety risks. The plans demonstrated strengths in technical root cause identification, the use of a single-screen test before full system restoration, and a factual holding statement to media. However, the response was delayed in key areas: Unified Command was not activated until under pressure from airlines, the PA was not silenced promptly, and the Incident Action Log was not maintained in real time. The failure to verify gate data against the official list led to a wasted police deployment to a non-existent gate. These issues point to systemic gaps in command structure, communication protocols, and backup system awareness. The most critical changes involve establishing command early, enforcing real-time documentation, and validating all data inputs against official sources.

capabilities.ratingRationale: The capability was performed with some challenges. The PIO issued a holding statement within 10 minutes of the media call, which was timely and factual, but failed to issue a correction within 15 minutes of the PA announcement about Flight 666 to Purgatory. The first social media post on the cyberattack rumor was delayed by 30 minutes and did not address the misinformation. Coordination with IT was not established before the first post, and the PIO waited for IT to initiate contact.

strengths.title: Media Holding Statement
strengths.analysisMd: The PIO issued a holding statement to Channel 5 News within 10 minutes of the call, confirming a disruption and an ongoing investigation without speculating on the cause. The statement was reviewed by the Ops Director and IT Director, ensuring factual accuracy and consistency with the airport's public messaging policy. This prevented premature speculation and maintained credibility.

No public statement was issued within 15 minutes of the announcement to clarify that the flight was not real and that there was no physical threat. The first public post was issued at 1:50, 35 minutes after the announcement, and only acknowledged display problems without addressing the false flight. This delay allowed misinformation to spread and undermined public trust.

correctiveActions.action: Add a mandatory 15-minute public statement trigger to the TIRP 13.7 Checklist for any PA or FIDS announcement involving passenger movement or flight status.

areasForImprovement.title: Uncoordinated Public Messaging with IT
areasForImprovement.analysisMd: The PIO did not coordinate with the IT Director before issuing the first social media post. The PIO assumed IT would notify them, but IT did not initiate contact. This gap in communication led to a delayed and incomplete public statement. The PIO should not wait for IT to confirm the nature of the failure before issuing a public statement, especially when misinformation is spreading.

This confirmed that the decision to 'Go Dark' was based on a risk assessment that prioritized life safety over operational continuity, as required by AEP 4.1.

Conduct a biannual drill to test the Crash Phone and mass notification system, with a focus on rapid deployment.
